officialTitle: Adjuvant paclitaxel and trastuzumab for node-negative, HER2-positive breast cancer

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: We performed an uncontrolled, single-group, multicenter, investigator-initiated study of adjuvant paclitaxel and trastuzumab in 406 patients with tumors measuring up to 3 cm in greatest dimension.
design.notes: Weekly paclitaxel and trastuzumab for 12 weeks followed by 9 months of trastuzumab monotherapy. Phase classification per trial design (single-arm phase 2).

clinicalQuestion: Is a de-escalated regimen of weekly paclitaxel plus trastuzumab associated with a low recurrence risk in small, node-negative HER2-positive breast cancer?

pico.population: Small (≤3 cm), node-negative HER2-positive breast cancer
pico.intervention: Weekly paclitaxel plus trastuzumab for 12 weeks, then trastuzumab to complete 1 year
pico.outcomes: Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: toxicity

arms.label: Paclitaxel + trastuzumab
arms.regimen: Weekly paclitaxel and trastuzumab for 12 weeks, then trastuzumab monotherapy for 9 months

publications.title: Adjuvant paclitaxel and trastuzumab for node-negative, HER2-positive breast cancer.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: The median follow-up period was 4.0 years. The 3-year rate of survival free from invasive disease was 98.7% (95% confidence interval [CI], 97.6 to 99.8).

safety.sourceQuote: A total of 13 patients (3.2%; 95% CI, 1.7 to 5.4) reported at least one episode of grade 3 neuropathy, and 2 had symptomatic congestive heart failure (0.5%; 95% CI, 0.1 to 1.8)
A total of 13 patients (3.2%; 95% CI, 1.7 to 5.4) reported at least one episode of grade 3 neuropathy, and 2 had symptomatic congestive heart failure (0.5%; 95% CI, 0.1 to 1.8)

strengths: Addresses a population largely excluded from pivotal adjuvant trastuzumab trials
Very low event rate with a simple, less toxic regimen
limitations: Single-group, non-randomised design without a comparator
Few events limit precision for higher-risk subsets

clinicalImplications.text: Supports weekly paclitaxel plus trastuzumab as a de-escalated adjuvant option for small, node-negative HER2-positive breast cancer.

tumourBoardPearl.text: For predominantly stage I HER2-positive disease, APT offers an anthracycline-free, single-taxane approach — the evidence is single-arm, so reserve it for genuinely low-risk tumours.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 25564897. Longer-term APT updates not yet ingested.
